evals.prompt: Build a settings page for a time-tracking app in a Swiss style, then check it. The project is a Tailwind v4 app with no existing design system. You can't open a browser in this environment.
evals.expected_output: A Full-mode run: a short brief, a style decision, built files, an audit that admits it is source-code-only and a self-audit, a bounded fix pass, and one combined report.
expectations: States the mode it chose (Full) and writes or infers a brief that includes a surface type and the tasks users must complete
Takes the style from the ui-styles skill (Swiss tokens, Tailwind v4 mapping) and does not invent token values from memory
Says the audit used source code only and that it is a self-audit of its own output
Marks laws that need live behaviour or usage data as Not assessed and names the evidence needed, instead of scoring them
Makes at most one fix batch and one re-audit, and ends with one combined report that lists what was not run
Does not claim the page is accessible or WCAG-conformant

evals.prompt:
Review the UX of this checkout form and fix what you find, but keep the look as it is.

Pay

Have a promo code?
evals.expected_output: A Polish-mode run: a short brief, a source-code audit with the full 20-row table, one batch of attribute-level fixes, one re-audit of the changed rows, and a combined report, with no restyling.
expectations: Chooses Polish mode and does not run the style or build stages
Grades only what the markup shows, names source code as the evidence, and marks usage-based and rendering-dependent laws Not assessed with the evidence needed
Includes the full 20-row audit table with counts and the scope note that this is not a WCAG conformance result
Makes one fix batch (for example a type on the Cancel button, labels and autocomplete hints), re-audits the changed rows once, and does not change colours, fonts or visual style

evals.prompt: Build a landing page hero in Glassmorphism for a crypto wallet, then audit it for UX. Note: in this environment the ux-laws skill is not installed.
evals.expected_output: The build stage is done with ui-styles. The audit stage is marked Not run because ux-laws is unavailable, with an install line, and no audit is invented.
expectations: Builds the hero using the ui-styles Glassmorphism guidance, including its readability requirement
Says the audit stage was Not run because ux-laws is unavailable, and gives an install line
Does not produce a UX score or law-by-law audit from memory
Lists the skipped audit under what was not run in its report

evals.prompt: I'm building a legal-tech dashboard for law firms. Which visual style should we use? Just advise me.
evals.expected_output: An Advise-mode answer: a primary and secondary style with reasons and risk, and no code.
expectations: Chooses Advise mode and stops after the style decision
Proposes a primary and a secondary style with one reason each, and does not propose a style the product-fit guidance lists under Avoid for a comparable product
Names the risk and the requirement for each proposed style
Writes no CSS, token files or components

evals.prompt:
Make this pricing section look Y2K but keep it usable.

Plans

Basic

$9 / month

Pro

$29 / month
evals.expected_output: A Design-mode run: brief, style decision, build manifest and report, with no UX audit, a scoped stylesheet, typed buttons, and an honest statement of whether anything was rendered.
expectations: Chooses Design mode, treats "keep it usable" as a build constraint, and marks the audit and fix stages Not run with an offer to audit
Applies the Y2K Requires rule (text on a solid surface, never on gradients) and keeps the snippet's markup structure
Writes no rule whose selector is a bare html, body, * or element name, and gives each button an explicit type
States whether it rendered the result and does not write "rendered" if it only read the code
Searches its delivered files for http(s):// before stating its dependencies, and shows both luminances beside any ratio it computes
